d: The legendary Phantom 'Cuda returns to the graveyard for modifications, and a delivery to a new owner in Switzerland! Prompting Mark and the Ghoulz to revisit the car, and the impossible restoration, that started the Graveyard Carz TV show!
Experience the meticulous, multi-stage resurrection, of the EV2 Hemi Orange 1969 440 Magnum Daytona. And the reveal of this ultra-rare, near survivor quality car, to the only owners it ever had!

Will prepares the legendary Phoenix 'Cuda for final paint in B5 blue, while Mark and Doug test-fire the 'Cuda's numbers matching 426 Hemi engine! The 1968 Road Runner gets its headliner installed  meanwhile, Mark, Royal, and Doug install the numbers matching 426 Hemi into the Phoenix 'Cuda!

A detailed look at the multi-stage resurrection, of a very rare 1969 B5 blue GTX! Watch as Mark and Doug make Graveyard Carz history, by delivering the GTX to its owners at their home! A very unique car and a very personal reveal.

Jack Curtis' 1968 roadrunner is completed! After purchasing this car in 1968, Jack and his wife raised their family with this beautiful Bright Blue Metallic muscle car as their daily driver. Making memories on family vacations, and even transporting livestock in the back seat! Join the Curtis family and their friends, as they react to the arrival, and welcome home their long awaited family car.

Mark examines the most documented car in the history of Graveyard Carz! From the dealership to the Graveyard, Mark has all the evidence he needs to bring this one owner, 1968 GTX, back to its former glory. But when he directs Will to paint a car an unoriginal color, Will cites some evidence of his own, to show that Mark is not the O.E.M. man he used to be.

Known as Moulin Rouge in the Plymouth line-up, and Panther Pink on a Dodge, FM3 is a 1970 only color, that is highly sought after by collectors. Three real FM3 pink Mopars are featured: A look back at a Super Bee from the very first episode of Graveyard Carz, a deep dive on a very rare Challenger, and finally, the restoration and delivery of a very unique 1970 'Cuda in perfectly painted FM3 Moulin

Mark proves the naysayers wrong, when he shows how the corpse of a decaying Dodge will save a customer's cherished Charger. Will and his protege, primer and paint a 1970 roadrunner convertible. Prompting Mark and Will to discuss the finer points of painting pedagogy. Or more importantly, which of them is the better teacher?
